problem: VLN pretraining relies on small human-labeled datasets or out-of-domain image-caption data (e.g. Conceptual Captions, Airbnb), leaving a domain gap to trajectory-instruction pairs and weak generalization to unseen scenes. Full finetuning of large pretrained models is also slow.
motivation: Human annotation of navigation trajectories is costly and existing datasets are small. CLIP holds strong vision-language alignment knowledge that can label rooms/objects in navigation views without human labeling. Prompt tuning could adapt a pretrained model to VLN with less training.
key_idea: Self-explore training environments by sampling trajectories, use CLIP to name rooms and objects at each viewpoint, fill masked instruction templates with those phrases and first-person actions to build in-domain data, then pretrain a ViLBERT-like model with prompt tuning.
insight: In-domain synthetic data built from CLIP labels matters: in the R2R ablation, prompt-tuning pretraining on the generated data raises val-unseen SR from 39.5 (ranking-only baseline) to 60.3, above finetuning on R2R (59.3). Data-generation ablations show that matching the template's mask count to the number of viewpoints and using Matterport room/object classes (rather than Places365/Objects365) give better SR (50.7 vs 49.4 and 48.9 on val-unseen).
method: Template generation: mask noun phrases (O_mask) and action words such as left/right/forward/around (A_mask) in R2R human instructions to obtain reusable templates

Trajectory sampling: randomly sample start/end points in Matterport3D training environments with fewer than 8 hops; derive first-person actions (forward/around/right+forward etc.) from headings and elevations

CLIP phrase matching: score 'a photo of [c]' against each view for Matterport room and object classes; take the top room and top object, written randomly as '[room]', '[object]' or '[room] with [object]'

Template filling: pick a template whose O_mask count matches the number of viewpoints, fill objects with sampled captions, and fill A_mask with the action between the corresponding viewpoints; about 50k pairs generated

Prompt-based architecture: ViLBERT-like model with a prompt encoder (BiLSTM + 2-layer ReLU MLP) whose continuous prompt vectors are prepended to the text embeddings. Only the prompt encoder and visual embeddings are trained in pretraining, and the text encoder is frozen

Pretraining and adaptation: ranking loss over hard-negative paths (10 epochs) then discriminative fine-tuning (20 epochs); generative setting follows Recurrent VLN-BERT, with the prompt encoder added and the whole model unfrozen

setting.backbone: ViLBERT-like model with prompt encoder (BiLSTM+MLP), used in Recurrent VLN-BERT generative agent; CLIP (frozen) for data generation
setting.training_data: About 50k self-generated instruction-trajectory pairs (CLIP-labeled templates in Matterport training environments), then R2R / REVERIE training data; initialized from ViLBERT pretrained weights
setting.observation: panoramic RGB (36 views) with orientation features

numbers.extra: pretrained on 50k generated pairs, no speaker-augmented data

Results by comparing ProbES with VLN-BERT in discriminative setting

results: With generative Recurrent VLN-BERT, ProbES reaches R2R val-unseen SR 61 / SPL 55 and test SR 62 / SPL 56. It slightly beats VLN-BERT (SR 60, SPL 55 on val-unseen) but trails Rec (PREVALENT) (SR 63, SPL 57). On REVERIE it gives the best RGS/RGSPL on val-unseen and test-unseen (16.84/13.94 and 15.11/12.32), ahead of Rec (VLN-BERT). In the discriminative setting it improves SR from 59.26 to 60.28.
limitations: Gains over VLN-BERT are small, about 1 SR point on R2R val-unseen, and it does not beat Rec (PREVALENT) on R2R

Templates come from human-annotated R2R instructions, and generated instructions depend on CLIP recognizing only a fixed set of Matterport room/object labels, so the process is not fully free of human data
The claimed fast-adaptation advantage is not quantified with training-time numbers in the text
